questions.question: A trader buys 500 kg cotton for Rs. 8,000. If 10% of this cotton is spoiled due to rain, at what rate (Rs./kg) should he sell the rest to earn a 20% profit?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A trader buys 500 kg cotton for Rs. 8,000. 10% of this cotton is spoiled due to rain. He wants to earn a 20% profit.

**Formula Used:**

Profit Percentage (P%) = (Profit / Cost Price) × 100

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) + Profit

**Calculation:**

Total cotton = 500 kg

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 8,000

⇒ Spoiled cotton = 10% of 500 kg = 0.10 × 500 = 50 kg

⇒ Usable cotton = 500 kg - 50 kg = 450 kg

⇒ Desired Profit = 20%

⇒ Desired Profit Amount = 20% of Rs. 8,000 = 0.20 × 8,000 = Rs. 1,600

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = Rs. 8,000 + Rs. 1,600 = Rs. 9,600

⇒ Selling Price per kg = Total SP / Usable cotton

⇒ Selling Price per kg = Rs. 9,600 / 450 kg

⇒ Selling Price per kg = Rs. 21 (1/3)

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: A natural number n divides 732 and leaves 12 as a remainder. How many values of n are possible?
questions.solution:
Formula Used:

N = ap × bq × cr

The total number of factors = (p + 1) × (q + 1) × (r + 1)

Calculation: 

When 732 is divided by a positive integer x, the remainder is 12. So, 

732 – 12 = 720

So 720 will be completely divisible by x

720 = 24 × 32 × 51

Total number of factors of 720 = (4 + 1) × (2 + 1) × (1 + 1) = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30

Number of factors 12 or less than 12 are (10) = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12

So x cannot have these values because x is greater than 12

So, we can say that there are 30 - 10 = 20 possible values of x

questions.question: A covered wooden box has the inner measures as 128 cm, 90 cm, 25 cm and the thickness of wood is 5.5 cm. Find the volume of the wood.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a **covered box**, outer dimensions = inner dimensions + (2 × **thickness**).

Outer L, B, H = (128+11), (90+11), (25+11) = 139, 101, 36 cm.

**Volume of wood** = Outer Volume − Inner Volume.

Volume = (139 × 101 × 36) − (128 × 90 × 25) = 505404 − 288000.

**∴ The correct answer is 217404 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Inner Length (l) = 128 cm, Inner Breadth (b) = 90 cm, Inner Height (h) = 25 cm.

**Thickness of wood** (t) = 5.5 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of wood = (Outer Length × Outer Breadth × Outer Height) − (Inner Length × Inner Breadth × Inner Height)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a01636d604f3c067005244ea1288551e6dc2a1e979267e74d5165964de0c2fc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total increase in each dimension = 2 × 5.5 = 11 cm

⇒ **Outer Length** (L) = 128 + 11 = 139 cm

⇒ **Outer Breadth** (B) = 90 + 11 = 101 cm

⇒ **Outer Height** (H) = 25 + 11 = 36 cm

⇒ **Inner Volume** = 128 × 90 × 25 = 288000 cm³

⇒ **Outer Volume** = 139 × 101 × 36 = 505404 cm³

⇒ **Volume of Wood** = 505404 − 288000 = 217404 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 217404 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The volume of a **rectangular cuboid** is calculated as Length × Breadth × Height.

Open vs. Closed Box

For a **closed box**, add 2 × thickness to all dimensions. For an **open box**, add 2 × thickness to L and B, but only 1 × thickness to the Height.

Total Surface Area

The total surface area of a cuboid is 2(lb + bh + hl), where l, b, and h are its dimensions.</p

questions.question: Rohan can alone finish a work in 12 days and Hari can alone in 16 days. They both work for 3 days and then Rohan left. After that only Hari works and finishes the work. The total work will be completed in:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let T be the total duration of the work (time Hari worked).

Fractional work equation: (Rohan time ÷ Rohan total) + (Hari time ÷ Hari total) = 1.

(3 ÷ 12) + (T ÷ 16) = 1

1/4 + T/16 = 1 ⇒ T/16 = 3/4.

T = (3 × 16) ÷ 4 = 12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Rohan alone = 12 days, Hari alone = 16 days. They work together for 3 days.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

⇒ Total Work = LCM of 12 and 16 = 48 units.

⇒ Combined efficiency of Rohan and Hari = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day.

⇒ Work done in 3 days = 7 × 3 = 21 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 48 − 21 = 27 units.

⇒ Time taken by Hari alone to finish remaining work = 27 ÷ 3 = 9 days.

⇒ Total time to complete work = Initial 3 days + Hari's 9 days = 12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If a person is twice as efficient as another, they take half the time to complete the same work.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed according to the ratio of the actual work done by each individual (Efficiency × Time).

Pipes and Cisterns

This follows the same logic as Time and Work, where an outlet pipe (leak) has negative efficiency and reduces the total work done.</p

questions.question: If 6428A83 is divisible by 9, then the value of A is equal to :
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of digits of **6428A83** = 6 + 4 + 2 + 8 + A + 8 + 3 = **31 + A**.

According to the **Divisibility Rule of 9**, the sum of digits must be a multiple of 9.

The nearest multiple of 9 after 31 is **36**.

31 + A = 36 ⇒ A = **5**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given number:** 6428A83

**Property:** A number is divisible by 9 only if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 9.

⇒ Sum = 6 + 4 + 2 + 8 + A + 8 + 3

⇒ Sum = 31 + A

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 9, (31 + A) ÷ 9 must leave a **remainder of 0**.

⇒ Multiples of 9 are 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, ...

⇒ Since A is a single digit (0 to 9), the only possible value for 31 + A is 36.

⇒ 31 + A = 36

⇒ A = 36 − 31

⇒ A = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

Similar to 9, a number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the **sum of digits at odd places** and the **sum of digits at even places** is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Digital Root Concept

The **digital root** of a number is the single-digit sum obtained by adding digits repeatedly. For any number divisible by 9, the digital root is always 9.</p

questions.question: A cylinder has a curved surface area equal to 350% of the curved surface area of another cylinder. If their radii are in the ratio 3 : 1, then the volume of the smaller cylinder is approximately _____% of the larger cylinder (the smaller cylinder has its radius and height smaller when compared to the larger).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Radii (R : r)** = 3 : 1

Ratio of **CSA (C₁ : C₂)** = 350 : 100 = 3.5 : 1

Ratio of **Heights (H : h)** = (C₁/R) : (C₂/r) = (3.5/3) : (1/1) = 3.5 : 3

Ratio of **Volumes (V₁ : V₂)** = (R² × H) : (r² × h) = (3² × 3.5) : (1² × 3) = 31.5 : 3

Required percentage = (3 ÷ 31.5) × 100 = (1 ÷ 10.5) × 100 ≈ 9.52%

**∴ The correct answer is 9.52.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Radius ratio of **Larger (R)** to **Smaller (r)** cylinder = 3 : 1

⇒ CSA of Larger cylinder (CL) = 350% of CSA of Smaller cylinder (CS)

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh

⇒ Volume (V) = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90ab97aba5db37ea317adcf6905579255652eea18b6d45bb69a65c1d476dadcf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let R = 3x and r = x

⇒ CL = 3.5 × CS

⇒ 2πRH = 3.5 × 2πrh

⇒ 3x × H = 3.5 × x × h

⇒ H/h = 3.5/3 = 7/6

⇒ Volume of Larger Cylinder (VL) = πR²H = π(3x)²(7/6)h = π(9x²)(7/6)h = 10.5πx²h

⇒ Volume of Smaller Cylinder (VS) = πr²h = πx²h

⇒ Percentage = (VS / VL) × 100

⇒ Percentage = (πx²h / 10.5πx²h) × 100 = 100 / 10.5

⇒ Percentage = 1000 / 105 ≈ 9.52%

**∴ The correct answer is 9.52.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cylinder Properties

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a cylinder = 2πr(h + r). It includes both the curved surface and the two circular bases.

Volume and CSA Relationship

The volume of a cylinder can also be expressed as Volume = (CSA × r) ÷ 2. This is useful when CSA and radius are known.

Ratio Scaling

If radius is scaled by 'k' and height by 'm', the CSA scales by (k × m) and the volume scales by (k² × m).</p

questions.question: Two numbers are, respectively, 30% and 60% more than a third number. The ratio of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume the **third number** is 100.

Then the **first number** becomes 130 and the **second number** becomes 160.

The required **ratio** is 130 : 160.

Simplified ratio ⇒ 13 : 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 ∶ 16.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in first number = 30%

Increase in second number = 60%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b77fff67612c3910d6d17efe075a80dc5cc9ed4e8c0e32c0fa74d33c2a077d26.png] 

Let the **third number** be x.

⇒ **First number** = x + 30% of x = 1.3x

⇒ **Second number** = x + 60% of x = 1.6x

⇒ **Ratio** = First number / Second number

⇒ **Ratio** = 1.3x / 1.6x

⇒ **Ratio** = 13 / 16

**∴ The correct answer is 13 ∶ 16.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase Formula

New Value = Original Value × (1 + Rate/100). In this case, the third number acts as the **original base**.

Ratio Simplification

To simplify a ratio a : b, divide both terms by their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** to get the simplest form.

Comparing Percentages

When multiple values are compared to a common reference, that reference is often assumed as **100** for easier calculation.

questions.question: In what proportion must tea worth Rs. 27 and Rs. 31 per kg be mixed so as to gain 25% by selling the mixture at Rs. 36 per kg?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Tea worth Rs. 27 per kg and Rs. 31 per kg

Selling price of the mixture to gain 25% = Rs. 36 per kg

**Concept:**

We use the concept of alligation to find the ratio in which two varieties must be mixed.

**Formula Used:**

Alligation rule:

If two ingredients are mixed, then the ratio of the quantities of the two ingredients is given by:

⇒ (C₁ - Cₘ) : (Cₘ - C₂)

where C₁ and C₂ are the costs of the two ingredients, and Cₘ is the mean cost of the mixture.

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the mixture be Cₘ.

Given selling price of mixture = Rs. 36 per kg

Gain = 25%

⇒ Cost price of mixture (Cₘ) = Selling price / (1 + Gain)

⇒ Cₘ = 36 / (1 + 0.25)

⇒ Cₘ = 36 / 1.25

⇒ Cₘ = 28.8

Using the alligation rule:

⇒ (C₁ - Cₘ) : (Cₘ - C₂)

⇒ (31 - 28.8) : (28.8 - 27)

⇒ 2.2 : 1.8

⇒ 11 : 9

**∴ The correct answer is option 4 (11 ∶ 9).**

questions.question: The marked price of an item is 1.4 times the cost price. In order to earn 23.2% profit, what per cent discount can a shopkeeper allow?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The marked price (MP) of an item is 1.4 times the cost price (CP).

To earn a 23.2% profit, we need to find the discount percentage.

**Concept:**

Profit percentage (Profit%) = (Selling Price (SP) - Cost Price (CP)) / CP × 100

Discount percentage (Discount%) = (Marked Price (MP) - Selling Price (SP)) / Marked Price (MP) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 1.4 × CP

⇒ MP = 1.4 × 100 = 140 units

Profit% is 23.2%:

⇒ Profit = (SP - CP) / CP × 100

⇒ 23.2 = (SP - 100) / 100 × 100

⇒ 23.2 = SP - 100

⇒ SP = 123.2 units

Now, we calculate the discount percentage:

⇒ Discount% = (MP - SP) / MP × 100

⇒ Discount% = (140 - 123.2) / 140 × 100

⇒ Discount% = 16.8 / 140 × 100

⇒ Discount% = 0.12 × 100

⇒ Discount% = 12%

**∴ The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: A person saves 45% of his income. Next year, his income increases by 200%. He increases his savings by five times the previous year’s savings. By what percentage (correct to one place of decimal) has he increased/decreased his expenditure?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial **Income** be 100, so **Savings** = 45 and **Expenditure** = 55.

New **Income** = 100 + 200 = 300.

New **Savings** = 5 × 45 = 225.

New **Expenditure** = 300 − 225 = 75.

% Increase in **Expenditure** = (75 − 55) / 55 × 100 = 20 / 55 × 100 ≈ 36.4%.

**∴ The correct answer is Increased, 36.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Savings** = 45% of **Income**

**Income** increase = 200%

Final **Savings** = 5 × Initial **Savings**

**Formula Used:**

**Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**

Percentage Change = (Final − Initial) / Initial × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6808f5618c1a6a24e96fd9462b6c4b02108e2c52ff947e9e5ee63ead8c21d3fe.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Initial **Income** = 100

⇒ Initial **Savings** (S₁) = 45% of 100 = 45

⇒ Initial **Expenditure** (E₁) = 100 − 45 = 55

⇒ New **Income** (I₂) = 100 + (200% of 100) = 100 + 200 = 300

⇒ New **Savings** (S₂) = 5 × 45 = 225

⇒ New **Expenditure** (E₂) = 300 − 225 = 75

⇒ Increase in **Expenditure** = 75 − 55 = 20

⇒ Percentage Increase = (20 / 55) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 400 / 11 ≈ 36.36% ≈ 36.4%

**∴ The correct answer is Increased, 36.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Relationship

The fundamental relation is **Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**. Any change in one variable must be balanced by the others.

Percentage Increase vs "Increase by X times"

An increase of 200% means the new value is 300% of the original (Multiplier = 3). "Increases by 5 times" can sometimes be interpreted as the new value being 5 times the old one or adding 5 times the old value to itself.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% then by b%, the net change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%, though in **Income-Expenditure** problems, simple linear addition of components is used.</p

questions.question: The hypotenuse of a right triangle is 6m more than twice the shortest side. If the third side is 2 m less than the hypotenuse, find the area(in m²) of the triangle.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The hypotenuse of a right triangle is 6 m more than twice the shortest side. The third side is 2 m less than the hypotenuse.

**Concept:**

In a right triangle, the relationship between the sides is given by the Pythagorean theorem: a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse.

**Formula Used:**

Pythagorean theorem: a² + b² = c²

Area of the triangle: (1/2) × base × height

**Calculation:**

Let the shortest side be x m.

The hypotenuse = 2x + 6 m

The third side = (2x + 6) - 2 = 2x + 4 m

Using the Pythagorean theorem:

⇒ x² + (2x + 4)² = (2x + 6)²

⇒ x² + (4x² + 16x + 16) = (4x² + 24x + 36)

⇒ x² + 4x² + 16x + 16 = 4x² + 24x + 36

⇒ 5x² + 16x + 16 = 4x² + 24x + 36

⇒ x² - 8x - 20 = 0

Solving the quadratic equation x² - 8x - 20 = 0:

⇒ x = [8 ± sqrt((8)² - 4 × 1 × (-20))]/2 × 1

⇒ x = [8 ± sqrt(64 + 80)]/2

⇒ x = [8 ± sqrt(144)]/2

⇒ x = [8 ± 12]/2

⇒ x = 10 m (taking the positive value)

Hence, the shortest side is 10 m.

The hypotenuse = 2x + 6 = 2 × 10 + 6 = 26 m

The third side = 2x + 4 = 2 × 10 + 4 = 24 m

Area of the triangle:

⇒ (1/2) × base × height

⇒ (1/2) × 10 × 24

⇒ 120 m²

**∴ The area of the triangle is 120 m².**

questions.question: Find the length of the sides of a triangle, if its angles are in the ratio 2 ∶ 4 ∶ 6 and its circumradius is 12 cm.

a = 2R sin A

b = 2R sin B

c = 2R sin C

**Calculation:**

First, find the angles of the triangle:

⇒ Let the angles be 2x, 4x, 6x

⇒ 2x + 4x + 6x = 180° 

⇒ 12x = 180° 

⇒ x = 15° 

Thus, the angles are:

⇒ A = 2x = 30° 

⇒ B = 4x = 60° 

⇒ C = 6x = 90° 

Now, use the circumradius R = 12 cm to find the sides:

⇒ a = 2 × 12 × \sin 30° 

⇒ a = 24 × 1/2

⇒ a = 12 cm

⇒ b = 2 × 12 × sin 60° 

⇒ b = 24 × √3/2

⇒ b = 12√3 cm

⇒ c = 2 × 12 × sin 90° 

⇒ c = 24 × 1

⇒ c = 24 cm

**∴ The lengths of the sides of the triangle are 12 cm, 12√3 cm, and 24 cm.**

questions.solution:
**Given:**

Illiterate female count in state C = 4,40,000

Illiterate ratio (M : F) in state C = 3 : 2

**Concept:**

Use the given ratio to find the total number of illiterate people, then use the literacy percentage to find the total population.

**Formula Used:**

Total illiterate population = Illiterate male + Illiterate female

Total population = Total illiterate population / (1 - Literacy percentage)

**Calculation:**

We have, illiterate female count = 4,40,000

Illiterate ratio (M : F) = 3 : 2

⇒ Let the number of illiterate males be 3x and females be 2x

⇒ 2x = 4,40,000

⇒ x = 4,40,000 / 2

⇒ x = 2,20,000

⇒ Number of illiterate males = 3x = 3 × 2,20,000

⇒ Number of illiterate males = 6,60,000

⇒ Total illiterate population = 6,60,000 + 4,40,000

⇒ Total illiterate population = 11,00,000

Literacy percentage in state C = 78%

⇒ Illiteracy percentage = 100% - 78% = 22%

⇒ Total population = Total illiterate population / Illiteracy percentage

⇒ Total population = 11,00,000 / 0.22

⇒ Total population = 50,00,000

**∴ The total population in state C is 50,00,000.**

questions.question: If the areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboid are 5 cm², 15 cm², 27 cm², respectively, the surface area of the cuboid is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a **cuboid**, the **Total Surface Area (TSA)** is equal to twice the sum of the areas of its three adjacent faces.

Adjacent face areas (x, y, z) = 5 cm², 15 cm², and 27 cm².

Total Surface Area = 2 × (x + y + z)

Total Surface Area = 2 × (5 + 15 + 27) = 2 × 47 = 94 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 94 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of face 1 (length × width) = 5 cm²

Area of face 2 (width × height) = 15 cm²

Area of face 3 (length × height) = 27 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of a cuboid = 2(lw + wh + lh)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ac9cdfdbaa2a8ae8eb304252ce0088e139146945a17252eb45348cbc21d8b05.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three adjacent face areas be A₁, A₂, and A₃.

⇒ A₁ = 5 cm², A₂ = 15 cm², A₃ = 27 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (A₁ + A₂ + A₃)

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (5 + 15 + 27)

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × 47

⇒ Total Surface Area = 94 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 94 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume from Face Areas

The **volume (V)** of a cuboid with adjacent face areas x, y, and z is given by V = √(x × y × z).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the **longest diagonal** is calculated using the formula D = √(l² + w² + h²).

Lateral Surface Area

The **Lateral Surface Area (LSA)**, which excludes the top and bottom faces, is given by 2h(l + w).</p

questions.question: If cot alpha=(P)/(Q), then find the value of (P cos alpha-Q sin alpha)/(P cos alpha+Q sin alpha) - (P²-Q²)/(P²+Q²)+3.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Divide the first term by **sin α** to convert it into **cot α**.

(P cot α − Q) ÷ (P cot α + Q) = (P × (P/Q) − Q) ÷ (P × (P/Q) + Q) = (P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²).

The total expression becomes [(P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)] − [(P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)] + 3.

The identical fraction terms cancel each other out, leaving only the constant.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cot α = P/Q

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b5f04612c2fd5521439c848837fe7bdb5a4a0db5637beb65ecc727d3bfe7b27.png] 

**Formula Used:** cot α = cos α ÷ sin α

⇒ Let the expression be E = [(P cos α − Q sin α) ÷ (P cos α + Q sin α)] − [(P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)] + 3

⇒ Divide the numerator and denominator of the first term by sin α:

⇒ Term 1 = [P(cos α ÷ sin α) − Q(sin α ÷ sin α)] ÷ [P(cos α ÷ sin α) + Q(sin α ÷ sin α)]

⇒ Term 1 = (P cot α − Q) ÷ (P cot α + Q)

⇒ Substitute cot α = P/Q into Term 1:

⇒ Term 1 = [P × (P/Q) − Q] ÷ [P × (P/Q) + Q]

⇒ Term 1 = [(P² − Q²) ÷ Q] ÷ [(P² + Q²) ÷ Q]

⇒ Term 1 = (P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)

⇒ Substitute Term 1 back into the original expression E:

⇒ E = [(P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)] − [(P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)] + 3

⇒ E = 0 + 3 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratio Identities

Fundamental identities include tan α = sin α ÷ cos α and cot α = cos α ÷ sin α = 1 ÷ tan α.

Pythagorean Identity

For any angle α, sin²α + cos²α = 1, which implies cos α = P ÷ √(P²+Q²) and sin α = Q ÷ √(P²+Q²) based on the right triangle.

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If a ÷ b = c ÷ d, then (a + b) ÷ (a − b) = (c + d) ÷ (c − d). This is often used to simplify ratio-based trigonometric equations.</p

questions.question: The length of a rectangular shaped park exceeds its breadth by 15 m. If the perimeter of the park is 110 m, find the length of the park (in m).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Sum** of Length (L) and Breadth (B) = Perimeter ÷ 2 = 110 ÷ 2 = 55 m.

**Difference** between Length and Breadth (L − B) = 15 m.

To find the **larger value (Length)**, use the formula: (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2.

⇒ Length = (55 + 15) ÷ 2 = 70 ÷ 2 = 35 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Perimeter** of the rectangular park = 110 m

**Length (L)** exceeds **Breadth (B)** by 15 m → L = B + 15

**Formula used:**

Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37331e2052fd8e95dd25231856d2393382ae4b48709ecd93bf47ea39d01934fd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (L + B) = 110

⇒ L + B = 110 ÷ 2

⇒ L + B = 55

⇒ Substituting L = B + 15 in the equation:

⇒ (B + 15) + B = 55

⇒ 2B + 15 = 55

⇒ 2B = 55 − 15

⇒ 2B = 40

⇒ B = 20 m

⇒ Length (L) = B + 15 = 20 + 15 = 35 m

**∴ The correct answer is 35 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space occupied by the rectangle is given by **Area = Length × Breadth**. For this park, Area = 35 × 20 = 700 m².

Diagonal of Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners is calculated using the **Pythagoras theorem**: Diagonal = √(L² + B²).

Semi-Perimeter

The sum of one length and one breadth (L + B) is known as the **semi-perimeter**, which is exactly half of the total perimeter.</p
